question:
DRAG DROP -
An engineer must configure the HSRP protocol to implement redundancy using two Cisco Nexus Series switches. In addition, the HSRP implementation must meet these requirements:
* switch1 must retain the primary role if switch2 goes offline.
* switch1 must retain the primary role until normal conditions are restored.
* switch1 and switch2 must ensure that the routing tables are converged before taking the active role.
* switch2 must retain the primary role if the default gateway is not reachable.
Drag and drop the configuration commands from the right to the left to meet the requirements. The commands are used more than once. Not all commands are used.
template:
! switch1
track 100 ip route 0.0.0.0/0 reachability

interface ethernet 1/1
ip 209.165.200.226/27

hsrp 200
ip 209.165.200.225
priority 210
{{1}}
{{2}}

no shutdown

! switch2
track 100 ip route 0.0.0.0/0 reachability

interface ethernet 1/1
ip 209.165.200.227/27

hsrp 200
ip 209.165.200.225
{{3}}
{{4}}

no shutdown
theory: Object tracking on HSRP lets a router lower its own priority (via a "track ... decrement") when a tracked condition (like default-route reachability) fails, so the peer with intact reachability becomes/stays active instead. "preempt delay minimum" forces a router that regains a higher priority to wait a configured number of seconds before reclaiming the active role, giving routing protocols time to reconverge first — which is exactly what's needed so switch1 retains primary status until conditions are truly stable, and switch2 only takes over if the gateway itself becomes unreachable. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — HSRP Object Tracking and Preemption)
